name: Arizona

agency.name: Arizona Department of Transportation, Motor Vehicle Division

handbook.title: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide

knowledgeTest.format: 30 multiple-choice questions taken on a touch-screen computer at an MVD office (audio version available; walk-in, no appointment). Teens under 18 may instead take the Permit Test @ Home online through a parent/guardian's AZ MVD Now account or a participating driving school.
knowledgeTest.languages: English, Arabic, French, German, Italian, Korean, Mandarin, Russian, Spanish, Tagalog, Vietnamese; verbal test by appointment for applicants who cannot read well.
knowledgeTest.retestWait: Not clearly stated on current ADOT pages. A 2014 ADOT news release set a minimum 7-day wait after a failed written or road test; the current Motorcycle License page says one application fee covers attempts within 12 months and you can retest the next day. For the Permit Test @ Home, additional attempts need no additional fee.
knowledgeTest.notes: Same 30-question test for all ages; score of 80% (24/30) required. Anyone who has never held a U.S. license must pass it. Instruction permit at 15 years 6 months (Class G permit) or 18 (operator permit); under-18 applicants need parent/guardian signature. The Permit Test @ Home (under 18, $7 fee) has a 30-minute limit per ADOT's FAQ flyer 15-0701; no time limit is published for the office test. Office testing 7:30 a.m.-4:45 p.m. Mon-Fri except holidays and the second Wednesday of each month.

facts.detail: Drivers 21 and older lose their driving privilege on the spot if a test shows an alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent or more. You can still be found guilty of DUI below 0.08 if impaired.

source.quote: If you are stopped for driving under the influence and a test shows that you have an alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent or more (0.04 in a commercial vehicle requiring a commercial driver license), you will lose your driving privilege on the spot.

facts.value: Any alcohol concentration (zero tolerance)
facts.detail: Arizona is 'Under 21 = ZERO Tolerance': a driver under 21 can have the license suspended for any alcohol concentration. The manual also states any trace of alcohol or impairing drugs brings a 2-year license suspension for drivers under 21.

source.quote: If you are under 21, your license may be suspended if there is any alcohol concentration.

facts.value: 0.04% BAC (in a commercial vehicle)
facts.detail: The limit is 0.04 when driving a commercial vehicle that requires a CDL, half the 0.08 adult limit.

source.quote: If you are stopped for driving under the influence and a test shows that you have an alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent or more (0.04 in a commercial vehicle requiring a commercial driver license), you will lose your driving privilege on the spot.

facts.value: 12-month suspension for a first refusal (24 months for a second refusal within 84 months)
facts.detail: By driving in Arizona you consent to blood, breath, urine or other testing if arrested for DUI. Refusing or not completing the test means automatic loss of the driving privilege for 12 months; a second refusal within 84 months (7 years) means 24 months.

source.quote: If you refuse to submit to or do not successfully complete any tests when you are arrested for driving under the influence, you will automatically lose your driving privilege for 12 months, or 24 months for a second refusal within 84 months.

facts.value: At least 10 consecutive days jail, license suspended at least 90 days, fine at least $1,250
facts.detail: A first DUI also requires alcohol screening/education/treatment and community service, and the court may order a Certified Ignition Interlock Device.

source.quote: First offense – you will be jailed for not less than 10 consecutive days, your driver license will be suspended for not less than 90 days, and you will be assessed a fine of not less than$1,250.

facts.value: No open container of alcohol for driver or passengers in the passenger compartment
facts.detail: The passenger compartment includes unlocked compartments within reach; the trunk (or area behind the last upright seat) is not included. Passengers in a bus, limousine, taxi or motor-home living area are exempt.

source.quote: It is illegal for a driver or passenger to consume or possess an open container of spirituous liquor in the passenger compartment of a motor vehicle while on any public roadway.

facts.value: 15 years 6 months
facts.detail: You may get a graduated (Class G) or motorcycle instruction permit at 15 years and 6 months after passing the written test. An operator (Class D) permit requires age 18. Permits are valid for 12 months.

source.quote: If you are at least 15 years and 6 months of age you may be issued a graduated and/or a motorcycle instruction permit.

facts.value: 6 months
facts.detail: Teens must hold the Arizona instruction permit at least 6 months (or until age 18) before getting a graduated license, and the permit must still be valid. Time held on another state's permit is credited.

source.quote: An applicant for a graduated license must have held an Arizona instruction permit for at least 6 months.

facts.value: 30 hours including 10 at night (or 20 hours with 6 at night after Traffic Survival School/Defensive Driving course)
facts.detail: Instead of completing an MVD-approved driver education program, a parent or guardian certifies in writing 30 supervised hours (10 at night), or 20 hours (6 at night) if the teen completed a Traffic Survival School or Defensive Driving course.

source.quote: the parent or guardian must certify in writing that the applicant either has completed at least 30 hours of supervised driving practice, including at least 10 hours at night

facts.value: Class A, B, C or D licensed driver at least 21, in the seat beside you
facts.detail: A graduated or operator permit holder must be accompanied by a licensed driver (Class A, B, C or D) who is at least 21 and sits in the seat beside the driver.

source.quote: Graduated or operator permit: you must be accompanied by a Class A, B, C or D licensed driver at least 21 years of age, who occupies the seat beside you.

facts.detail: The graduated (Class G) license is issued to applicants at least 16 but under 18 who have held a permit 6 months and completed driver education or certified practice.

source.quote: A graduated driver license is issued to an applicant who is at least 16, but less than 18, years of age

facts.value: No driving midnight to 5:00 a.m. for the first 6 months
facts.detail: Exceptions: a parent or legal guardian with a valid Class A, B, C or D license in the front passenger seat, or driving directly to/from a sanctioned school-sponsored activity, work, a sanctioned religious activity or a family emergency.

source.quote: For the first 6 months, a driver with a graduated driver license shall not drive a motor vehicle between the hours of midnight and 5:00 a.m. unless:

facts.value: No more than one passenger under 18 for the first 6 months
facts.detail: Exceptions: the passengers are the teen driver's siblings, or a parent or legal guardian with a valid Class A, B, C or D license occupies the front passenger seat.

source.quote: For the first 6 months, a driver with a graduated driver license shall not drive a motor vehicle containing more than one passenger under the age of 18, unless:

facts.detail: The unrestricted operator license (Class D) requires age 18. A graduated license holder may keep the Class G license after 18 or choose to get a Class D.

source.quote: You must be at least 18 years of age to apply for an operator license.

facts.value: Hand-held ban for all drivers
facts.detail: Arizona drivers may not hold or support a wireless device while driving; hands-free and voice-to-text use is allowed, and a device may be used to report an emergency.

source.quote: Arizona law prohibits holding or supporting a wireless device while driving.

facts.value: No writing or reading texts; no watching, recording or broadcasting video while driving
facts.detail: Applies to all drivers. Voice-to-text and hands-free operation are permitted.

source.quote: Drivers may not write or read any text-based communication while driving, and may not watch, record, or broadcast video while driving.

facts.value: Graduated licensees: no cell phone/wireless device use for the first 6 months
facts.detail: During the first 6 months with a graduated (Class G) license, wireless devices may not be used while driving except in emergencies or to operate an audible navigation system (no programming while driving).

source.quote: Cell phones and other wireless communication devices cannot be used while driving except in emergencies or to operate an audible navigation system (programming while driving is prohibited).

facts.value: All front-seat occupants must be belted; driver must make passengers under 16 buckle up
facts.detail: Each front-seat occupant must wear a properly adjusted and fastened lap/shoulder belt (or lap belt if that is all that is installed) while the vehicle is moving, and the driver must require all passengers under 16 to buckle up.

source.quote: The operator of a motor vehicle must require all passengers under the age of 16 years to buckle up.

facts.value: Under 5: child restraint; ages 5-7: child restraint until 4 feet 9 inches tall
facts.detail: Children under 5 must be in a child restraint system. Children 5 to 8 must stay in a child restraint system until they are at least 4'9" tall. Children 12 and under should never ride in the front seat.

source.quote: Arizona law requires that a person shall not operate a motor vehicle on the highways in this state when transporting a child who is under five years of age unless that child is properly secured in a child restraint system. Additionally, children between five and eight years of age are required to be in a child restraint system until they are a minimum of four feet, nine inches tall.

facts.value: Never faster than reasonable and prudent for conditions
facts.detail: Arizona's basic speed rule (A.R.S. 28-701) requires a speed that is reasonable and prudent for conditions and hazards, and controlled to avoid a collision. The manual says to reduce speed in bad weather and double following distance.

source.quote: A person shall not drive a vehicle on a highway at a speed greater than is reasonable and prudent under the circumstances, conditions and actual and potential hazards then existing.

facts.value: 15 mph
facts.detail: 15 mph when approaching a school crosswalk; the 15 mph maximum applies from the first school-crossing sign until past the crossing. Passing in a school crossing zone is prohibited, and you must stop when anyone is in the crosswalk.

source.quote: 15 mph when approaching a school crosswalk.

facts.value: 25 mph
facts.detail: Unless posted otherwise, the limit in any business or residential district is 25 mph.

source.quote: 25 mph in any business or residential district.

facts.value: 25 mph
facts.detail: Unless posted otherwise, the limit in any business or residential district is 25 mph.

source.quote: 25 mph in any business or residential district.

facts.value: 55 mph on open highways (65 mph on designated open highways) when not posted
facts.detail: The manual's unposted limits: 55 mph on open highways or city freeways, 65 mph on designated open highways, 75 mph on rural freeways. Always obey posted signs.

source.quote: 55 mph on open highways or city freeways.

facts.value: 75 mph on rural freeways
facts.detail: The manual lists 75 mph as the limit on rural freeways when no other limit is posted.

source.quote: 75 mph on rural freeways.

facts.value: Do not drive so slowly that you impede traffic
facts.detail: Driving too slowly is as dangerous as driving too fast; when slower than surrounding traffic, keep right and let faster vehicles pass.

source.quote: Driving too slowly can be as dangerous as driving too fast. Remember to drive in the right lane and allow faster moving vehicles to pass whenever you are driving slower than traffic around you.

facts.value: Allowed after a complete stop unless a sign prohibits it
facts.detail: Stop completely before the marked or unmarked crosswalk, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and oncoming traffic, and turn into the right lane unless signs direct otherwise.

source.quote: Where not prohibited by signs, a right turn may be made after coming to a complete stop, when motor traffic and pedestrian traffic are clear.

facts.value: Only from a one-way road onto a one-way road, after stopping and yielding
facts.detail: A left turn on red is allowed only from a one-way road into a one-way road (unless signs prohibit). A left turn from a one-way road onto a two-way road cannot be made on red.

source.quote: This is the only left turn situation where, unless signs prohibit it, you may make the turn against a red light after stopping and yielding to traffic and pedestrians.

facts.value: At least 100 feet (about 4 seconds) before turning
facts.detail: Signal at least 100 feet before a turn. If turning just beyond an intersection, wait until you are in the intersection to signal.

source.quote: Signal at least 100 feet (approximately 4 seconds) before you turn so other drivers will have time to react.

facts.value: Yield, pull to the right and stop; stay 500 ft behind fire vehicles and 300 ft behind police vehicles
facts.detail: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights/siren, move right and stop until it passes. When following, stay at least 500 feet behind a responding fire vehicle and 300 feet behind a responding police vehicle, and do not drive or park within the block where it has stopped.

source.quote: The driver shall maintain a distance of at least 500 feet behind a fire department vehicle responding to an emergency and at least 300 feet behind a police vehicle responding to an emergency.

facts.value: Move over one lane for any stopped vehicle with flashing lights; if not possible, slow down
facts.detail: Arizona's Move Over Law (A.R.S. 28-775) covers all vehicles pulled over with flashing lights, including emergency vehicles, tow trucks, highway maintenance and private vehicles, on freeways, multi-lane highways and city streets.

source.quote: requires motorists to move over one lane to create a safe margin of space when driving by any vehicle with flashing lights pulled to the side of a road or highway. If it’s not safe or possible to move over, motorists must slow down and use caution.

facts.value: Stop for a loading school bus in either direction; no stop needed only on a physically divided roadway when going the opposite way
facts.detail: Stop before reaching a school bus with flashing lights and stop arm, regardless of direction, until it moves or the signals stop. On a divided roadway (fence, curbing or pavement separation) opposite-direction traffic need not stop; painted striping alone is not a divider.

source.quote: You are not required to stop for a school bus on a divided roadway when traveling in the opposite direction. A divided roadway is one in which the road is separated by physical barriers such as a fence, curbing or separation of the pavement. Roadway striping by itself does not constitute a physical separation of the roadway.

facts.value: At least 3 seconds (3 to 6 seconds; 6+ on slippery roads)
facts.detail: Use the 3-6 second rule: at least 3 seconds normally, more at higher speeds and in poor conditions; double to 6 seconds or more on slippery roads.

source.quote: Allow at least a 3-second following distance for most driving situations.

facts.value: Sunset to sunrise (and in low-visibility conditions)
facts.detail: Headlights are required from sunset to sunrise. Also turn on low beams in sun glare, rain, dust or any condition where your vehicle may not be clearly visible.

source.quote: You must use headlights from sunset to sunrise, but be aware that other driver may not have turned on their headlights.

facts.value: 500 feet
facts.detail: Use high beams on highways only when no oncoming vehicle is within 500 feet; switch to low beams when meeting oncoming traffic.

source.quote: Use high beams on highways when no other vehicle is coming toward you within 500 feet.

facts.value: 200 feet
facts.detail: Use low beams whenever you are within 200 feet of a vehicle you are following.

source.quote: When following another car, use low beams whenever you are within 200 feet.

facts.value: 15 feet
facts.detail: It is illegal to park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

source.quote: Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

facts.value: On a crosswalk or within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection
facts.detail: No parking on a crosswalk or within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.

source.quote: On a crosswalk or within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.

facts.value: Not within an intersection
facts.detail: Parking is illegal within the boundaries of an intersection (and within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection).

source.quote: Within the boundaries of an intersection.

facts.value: 30 feet on the approach to a stop sign, yield sign, flashing beacon or traffic signal
facts.detail: From A.R.S. 28-873 (the manual's parking list does not include this distance).

source.quote: Within thirty feet on the approach to any flashing beacon, stop sign, yield sign or traffic control signal located at the side of a roadway.

facts.value: 50 feet
facts.detail: It is illegal to park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.

source.quote: Within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.

facts.value: 20 feet from a fire station driveway (75 feet across the street when posted)
facts.detail: From A.R.S. 28-873 (not stated in the manual).

source.quote: Within twenty feet of the driveway entrance to a fire station and on the side of a street opposite the entrance to any fire station within seventy-five feet of the entrance when properly posted.

facts.value: Within 18 inches of the right-hand curb
facts.detail: From A.R.S. 28-874 (not stated in the manual).

source.quote: shall stop or park the vehicle with its right-hand wheels parallel to and within eighteen inches of the right-hand curb.

facts.value: No closer than 15 feet from the nearest track
facts.detail: Stop no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail when there are flashing red lights, a lowered barricade, ringing bells or a flagger. Never drive around or under a lowered gate.

source.quote: When you arrive at a railroad crossing, you must stop no closer than 15 feet from the nearest railroad track when you observe any of the following:

facts.value: At least 3 feet
facts.detail: Give at least 3 feet when passing a bicyclist going the same direction, and do not honk at bicyclists while passing.

source.quote: Motorists are required to allow a minimum safe distance of 3 feet when passing a bicyclist traveling in the same direction.

facts.value: Yield to pedestrians in any marked or unmarked crosswalk; never pass a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian
facts.detail: Even on a green light you must yield to pedestrians in the intersection, and you may not pass a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian even with a clear lane or green signal.

source.quote: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians crossing the street in any marked or unmarked crosswalk.

facts.value: Stay at the scene, help the injured, exchange information; call police immediately if anyone is injured
facts.detail: Exchange license number, name/address, insurance company and policy number, witness information and plate numbers. In a minor non-injury crash, move operable vehicles out of travel lanes (Quick Clearance).

source.quote: In case of injury, you are also required to immediately call the police.

facts.detail: Minimum Arizona liability: $25,000 bodily injury for one person, $50,000 for two or more persons, $15,000 property damage. Proof of insurance must be in the vehicle.

source.quote: $25,000 bodily injury liability for one person and $50,000 for two or more persons. • $15,000 property damage liability.

facts.value: 8 or more points in 12 months: Traffic Survival School or suspension
facts.detail: Points: DUI, extreme/aggravated DUI, reckless driving, racing and aggressive driving 8; leaving the scene 6; speeding 3; gore area 3; wrong-way driving 2; other moving violations 2.

source.quote: If you accumulate 8 or more points within any 12-month period, you are required to attend Traffic Survival School (TSS), or your driving privilege may be suspended.

facts.value: Helmet required for riders and passengers under 18
facts.detail: From A.R.S. 28-964 (not in the car manual). Riders 18 and older are not required to wear a helmet, but all operators need eye protection (glasses, goggles or face shield) unless the motorcycle has a protective windshield.

source.quote: An operator or passenger of a motorcycle, all-terrain vehicle or motor driven cycle who is under eighteen years of age shall wear at all times a protective helmet on the operator's or passenger's head in an appropriate manner.

facts.value: Lane filtering past stopped vehicles allowed: 2+ same-direction lanes, speed limit 45 mph or less, motorcycle 15 mph or less
facts.detail: Lane filtering applies only to passing vehicles stopped in the same direction. Otherwise riding between lanes is prohibited (A.R.S. 28-903). Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a lane.

source.quote: When it can be done safely, a motorcyclist may pass a vehicle that is stopped in the same direction and lane as the motorcycle, commonly known as lane filtering, provided that: • The street is divided into at least 2 adjacent lanes traveling in the same direction. • The posted speed limit does not exceed 45 miles per hour. • The motorcycle does not travel faster than 15 miles per hour.

notableLaws.title: Dust storms: Pull Aside, Stay Alive
notableLaws.summary: In a severe dust storm, slow down, drive completely off the highway, stop as far right as possible (not in a travel or emergency lane), turn off all lights, take your foot off the brake, and stay buckled in the vehicle until it passes.

source.quote: Drive completely off the highway. • Stop as far to the right as possible. • Do not stop in the travel lane or in the emergency lane. • Turn off your lights and take your foot off the brake. • Stay in the vehicle with your seat belts buckled.

notableLaws.title: Driving around flood barricades makes you pay for your rescue
notableLaws.summary: A driver who goes around barricades set up for flooding is liable for the cost of any emergency response needed to remove the driver or passengers from a stalled vehicle. Never cross flooded washes.

source.quote: A driver of a vehicle who drives around barricades set up due to flooding is liable for the expenses of any emergency response that is required to remove the driver or any passenger in the vehicle that becomes inoperable on a public street or highway.

notableLaws.title: Aggressive driving
notableLaws.summary: Aggressive driving = speeding plus two of: ignoring signs/signals, passing on the right, unsafe lane change, following too close, failing to yield to emergency vehicles, creating an immediate hazard. 1st offense: Traffic Survival School and possible 30-day suspension; 2nd within 24 months: Class 1 misdemeanor and 12-month suspension. 8 points.

source.quote: You may be cited for aggressive driving if you commit a series of acts during a single, continuous period of driving that presents an immediate hazard to another person or vehicle, exceed the posted speed limit and commit two of the following violations:

notableLaws.title: Extreme DUI (0.15+ BAC)
notableLaws.summary: Extreme DUI applies at 0.15 or higher: first offense at least 30 consecutive days in jail and at least a $2,500 fine; at 0.20 or higher, at least 45 days. An ignition interlock device is required.

source.quote: This category of DUI applies to a person with an alcohol concentration of 0.15 or higher.

notableLaws.title: Aggravated DUI (felony)
notableLaws.summary: DUI while suspended/revoked, a third DUI within 7 years, DUI with a passenger under 15, or DUI while required to use an ignition interlock is aggravated DUI: prison and a 1-year revocation.

source.quote: This category of DUI applies to a person who commits a DUI while their driving privilege is suspended or revoked, commits a third DUI in 7 years, or commits a DUI while a person under 15 is in the vehicle.

notableLaws.title: Red-light running requires Traffic Survival School
notableLaws.summary: Every red-light (or flashing red) conviction requires Traffic Survival School plus points; failing to complete TSS means indefinite suspension. Causing life-threatening injury: up to $500 fine and 3-month suspension; causing a death: up to $1,000 and 6-month suspension.

source.quote: MVD is required by law to order the completion of Traffic Survival School (TSS) for every red light conviction reported by the courts.

notableLaws.title: Fines double in work zones
notableLaws.summary: When signs are posted, fines for traffic violations, including speeding, are doubled in work zones.

source.quote: Fines double when traffic violations occur in work zones on Arizona streets and roadways.

notableLaws.title: Gore areas
notableLaws.summary: It is illegal to drive over or park in a gore area (the space between a through roadway and an entrance or exit ramp). Violation: 3 points.

source.quote: It is against the law to drive over or park in any part of a gore area.

notableLaws.title: HOV lanes
notableLaws.summary: During posted times Monday through Friday, freeway HOV lanes (white diamonds) are only for vehicles with two or more people (including the driver), motorcycles or buses.

source.quote: You may not drive a vehicle carrying fewer than two persons, including the driver, in an HOV lane at the posted times Monday through Friday.

notableLaws.title: Quick Clearance after minor crashes
notableLaws.summary: After a minor crash with no injuries, state law requires moving an operable vehicle out of the roadway if it can be moved safely. Moving it does not make you at fault.

source.quote: State law requires a driver involved in a minor crash without injuries to remove a vehicle from the roadway if it is operable and can be moved safely.

notableLaws.title: Leaving the scene of a crash
notableLaws.summary: Failure to stop: 1-year suspension (vehicle damage only); 3-year revocation (injury); 5-year revocation (serious physical injury); 10-year revocation (death). Leaving the scene carries 6 points.

source.quote: Suspended for 1 year if involving only damage to a vehicle.

notableLaws.title: No proof of insurance suspension
notableLaws.summary: A conviction for not having (or failing to produce) proof of insurance suspends the license, registration and plates: 3 months for a first violation, 6 months for a second within 36 months, 1 year for a third.

source.quote: A person that is convicted of not having or failing to produce evidence of current financial responsibility within the vehicle shall receive a suspension of the driving license, vehicle registration and license plates (as directed by the courts) for: • 3 months for a first violation.

gaps: knowledgeTest.retestWait: official pages conflict (2014 release: 7 days after a failed test; 2026 motorcycle page: retest the next day); not stated for the car test on current pages
motorcycleTest: ADOT publishes no question count or passing score for the motorcycle written test
parking_stop_sign_signal: not in the manual; sourced from A.R.S. 28-873
parking_fire_station: not in the manual; sourced from A.R.S. 28-873
parking_curb_distance: not in the manual; sourced from A.R.S. 28-874
motorcycle_helmet_law: not in the car manual; sourced from A.R.S. 28-964
basic_speed_law: manual has no single basic-speed-rule statement; sourced from A.R.S. 28-701
novice_phone_ban: not in the manual; sourced from ADOT Teen Driver Guide page (also A.R.S. 28-3174)
